newsitem.title: USA: Pilots reject new American Airlines pay offer.
newsitem.headline: Pilots reject new American Airlines pay offer.

text.p: Pilots at American Airlines Wednesday rejected a new pay offer designed to avert a strike threatened for midnight Friday.

Pilots union President James Sovich told reporters the offer was unacceptable and was worth less than the airlines' earlier offer. American, the nation's second-biggest carrier, had offered a raise of 6 percent over four years, up from 5 percent previously, but the offer also included changes in stock option plans. The Allied Pilots Association has asked for 11.5 percent.
The airline's new offer retained one stock option for the pilots but eliminated another. Sovich said the new offer was worth $43.1 million less than the airline's previous offer.
Airline officials said they were confused as to what the pilots wanted and that they did not know what formula the pilots used to calculate the value of the new offer.
Going into a fresh round of negotiations, one pilots union official said no counter offers were planned. He did not elaborate.

Aside from pay, also at issue is American Airlines' plan to use jets flown by lower-paid members of another union for its regional carrier, American Eagle. The airline says it needs this to remain competitive with other major U.S. carriers.
